candidate.title: Reschedule calendar update errors are swallowed: catch returns [] when calendarReference is unset and logs were removed
reports: packages/core/eventmanager.ts:592 — the catch block constructs message after its logger was removed, leaving dead diagnostic code while silently discarding the exception context.
packages/core/eventmanager.ts:596 — the console.error(message) in the reschedule catch block was removed, so calendar update failures during reschedule are swallowed with no log output

packages/core/eventmanager.ts:597 — if the throw happens before calendarreference is assigned (e.g. the prisma booking lookup fails) the catch returns an empty array, so callers see zero results and no failure signal at all

packages/core/eventmanager.ts:590 — promise.all(result) rejects on the first bad update, and the catch then reports every calendar reference as failed with credentialid 0, discarding the hosts whose update actually succeeded

packages/core/eventmanager.ts:593-607 — in the catch block, when error occurs before calendarreference is assigned, the function returns [] instead of a per-calendar failure result, so callers lose the error signal for user-facing error surfacing

packages/core/eventmanager.ts:604 — the catch block returns [] when calendarreference is undefined (e.g., error before references were computed), whereas it previously returned one failed result; callers expecting an error result now see silent success
candidate.example: eventmanager.ts:596 — console.error(message) removed from the catch block, so failures in updateallcalendarevents are swallowed with no log

fix_scope: minimal fix for the demonstrated instance only
